Changed for DuckDB: the PL/pgSQL functions became macros and statements, the foreign table became a view over the files found through Overture's STAC catalogue, sequences became row_number(), and the route is returned as rows so the map can draw it.

presets.label: Choose the area
sql: -- Adapted from overture.sql, the example code of Paul Ramsey's "Vehicle Routing with PostGIS and Overture Data": https://crunchydata.com/blog/vehicle-routing-with-postgis-and-overture-data
-- Next: “Latest Overture release”. After changing the area, run the presets again from here.
-- Playground: the area is a variable, and “Use this view” on the map rewrites the bbox line with
-- the map's view. overture.sql's box around Victoria, Canada (about 180 km²) is over the limit
-- below and slow to load in a browser, so this box of about 4 km covers central Hiroshima, from
-- Peace Memorial Park to Hiroshima Station.
SET VARIABLE bbox = {xmin: 132.44, ymin: 34.37, xmax: 132.48, ymax: 34.41};
-- Playground: “Load the area's segments” stops above this area. A browser's memory is the limit;
-- raise it with care.
SET VARIABLE max_area_km2 = 25;
-- Playground: the same approximation as the map's “Use this view” button.
WITH area AS (
SELECT (b.xmax - b.xmin) * 111.32 * cos(radians((b.ymin + b.ymax) / 2)) * (b.ymax - b.ymin) * 110.574 AS km2
FROM (SELECT getvariable('bbox') AS b)
SELECT round(km2, 1) AS area_km2, km2 <= getvariable('max_area_km2') AS within_limit
FROM area;

presets.label: Latest Overture release
sql: -- Next: “Segment files for the area”.
-- Playground: Overture removes each release about 60 days after it comes out, so the release is
-- looked up in Overture's STAC catalogue instead of being written into the SQL.
SET VARIABLE release = (SELECT latest FROM read_json('https://stac.overturemaps.org/catalog.json'));
SELECT getvariable('release') AS release;

presets.label: Segment files for the area
sql: -- Next: “Load the area's segments”.
-- DuckDB: overture.sql creates a foreign table over every segment file of one fixed release. This
-- view reads the latest release instead, and only the files whose bounding box meets the area:
-- Overture's STAC catalogue lists one box per file. Table functions take no subqueries, so the
-- lists pass through variables.
-- Playground: each check sets a variable rather than returning a row, because the Playground
-- shows the first result of a script.
SET VARIABLE area_set = (SELECT CASE WHEN getvariable('bbox') IS NULL
THEN error('Run the preset “Choose the area” first.') END);
SET VARIABLE release_set = (SELECT CASE WHEN getvariable('release') IS NULL
THEN error('Run the preset “Latest Overture release” first.') END);
SET VARIABLE items = (
WITH collection AS (
SELECT extent.spatial.bbox[2:] AS boxes, [l.href FOR l IN links IF l.rel = 'item'] AS items
FROM read_json('https://stac.overturemaps.org/' || getvariable('release') || '/transportation/segment/collection.json')
SELECT list(items[i] ORDER BY i)
FROM collection, range(1, len(boxes) + 1) AS t(i)
WHERE boxes[i][1] <= getvariable('bbox').xmax AND boxes[i][3] >= getvariable('bbox').xmin
AND boxes[i][2] <= getvariable('bbox').ymax AND boxes[i][4] >= getvariable('bbox').ymin
SET VARIABLE files_found = (SELECT CASE WHEN getvariable('items') IS NULL
THEN error('No Overture segment file covers this area.') END);
SET VARIABLE files = (SELECT list(assets.aws.href ORDER BY assets.aws.href) FROM read_json(getvariable('items')));
SET VARIABLE files_bbox = getvariable('bbox');
-- DuckDB: DuckDB-Wasm cannot convert the geometry of these GeoParquet files, so it is read as WKB
-- and converted with ST_GeomFromWKB in the next preset.
SET enable_geoparquet_conversion = false;
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW ov_segments AS
SELECT * FROM read_parquet(getvariable('files'));
SELECT unnest(getvariable('files')) AS file;

presets.label: Load the area's segments
sql: -- Takes about half a minute in a browser. Next: “Look at one segment”, or “Speed and cost macros”.
-- Create a local copy of the Overture data
-- so that it is easy to debug the attributes
-- of particular features (it is very very very
-- slow to directly pull one feature out of the
-- FDW tables with an id filter, because the
-- geoparquet files are not sorted by id)
-- Playground: stop with a plain error rather than load nothing. Each check sets a variable rather
-- than returning a row, because the Playground shows the first result of a script.
SET VARIABLE area_set = (SELECT CASE WHEN getvariable('bbox') IS NULL OR getvariable('max_area_km2') IS NULL
THEN error('Run the preset “Choose the area” first.') END);
SET VARIABLE files_current = (SELECT CASE WHEN getvariable('files') IS NULL OR getvariable('files_bbox') IS DISTINCT FROM getvariable('bbox')
THEN error('The area changed since the files were found; run “Segment files for the area” again.') END);
SET VARIABLE area_allowed = (SELECT CASE WHEN (b.xmax - b.xmin) * 111.32 * cos(radians((b.ymin + b.ymax) / 2)) * (b.ymax - b.ymin) * 110.574 > getvariable('max_area_km2')
THEN error(format('The area is {:.1f} km²; the limit is {} km².', (b.xmax - b.xmin) * 111.32 * cos(radians((b.ymin + b.ymax) / 2)) * (b.ymax - b.ymin) * 110.574, getvariable('max_area_km2'))) END
FROM (SELECT getvariable('bbox') AS b));
-- DuckDB: only the columns the next presets use, rather than *, so fewer bytes cross the network.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ov_segments_local AS
SELECT id, ST_GeomFromWKB(geometry) AS geometry, bbox, class, subclass, names, connectors,
road_surface, speed_limits, access_restrictions
FROM ov_segments
WHERE (bbox).xmin >= getvariable('bbox').xmin
AND (bbox).xmax <= getvariable('bbox').xmax
AND (bbox).ymin >= getvariable('bbox').ymin
AND (bbox).ymax <= getvariable('bbox').ymax;
SET VARIABLE roads_found = (SELECT CASE WHEN (SELECT count(*) FROM ov_segments_local) = 0
THEN error('No roads in this area.') END);
-- DuckDB: RAISE NOTICE's row count is this query's result.
SELECT count(*) AS rows_copied FROM ov_segments_local;

presets.label: Look at one segment
sql: -- Next: “Speed and cost macros”.
-- Check out what is in the FDW tables
-- use row_to_json() to surface the structure of the
-- nested data elements a little better than a raw * does
-- DuckDB: to_json() of the row, from the local copy.
SELECT to_json(s) AS segment
FROM ov_segments_local AS s
LIMIT 1 OFFSET 100;

presets.label: Speed and cost macros
sql: -- Next: “Chop segments into edges”.
-- Deal with kmph/mph units, and fill in any null
-- speed information with sensible defaults based
-- on the segment class.
-- DuckDB: the PL/pgSQL functions become scalar macros with the same rules.
CREATE OR REPLACE MACRO pgr_segment_kmph(speed, unit, class) AS
coalesce(
-- Convert mph to kmph where necessary
CASE WHEN unit = 'mph' THEN CAST(speed AS DOUBLE) * 1.60934 ELSE CAST(speed AS DOUBLE) END,
-- Apply some defaults
-- Should not be driving fast on service roads
CASE WHEN class = 'service' THEN 20
-- Or on residential roads
WHEN class = 'residential' THEN 30
-- Everywhere else, use the default
ELSE 40 END);
-- The cost to traverse a segment is the number of
-- seconds needed to traverse it, so distance over speed.
-- DuckDB: there is no geography type. ST_Length_Spheroid measures on the ellipsoid and reads
-- [latitude, longitude], so the coordinates are flipped first; the setting keeps that reading.
SET geometry_always_xy = false;
CREATE OR REPLACE MACRO pgr_segment_cost(geom, speed_kmph) AS
-- Geography length is in meters
ST_Length_Spheroid(ST_FlipCoordinates(geom))
-- Convert km/hour into meters/second
-- Segment cost is the number of seconds
-- needed to traverse the segment
-- Playground: 30 mph, a residential road without a limit, and 1.1 km at 36 km/h.
SELECT pgr_segment_kmph(30, 'mph', 'primary') AS kmph_for_30_mph,
pgr_segment_kmph(NULL, NULL, 'residential') AS kmph_residential,
round(pgr_segment_cost(ST_GeomFromText('LINESTRING(132.44 34.37, 132.44 34.38)'), 36), 1) AS seconds;

presets.label: Chop segments into edges
sql: -- Next: “Vertices from connectors”.
-- Create a simple table that reflects some of the
-- input we have generated (speed, directionality)
-- and just mirrors some other useful info (surface,
-- primary name) for mapping purposes.
-- Most importantly, carry out the chopping of segments
-- into edges with only two graph connectors, one at
-- the start and one at the end.
-- DuckDB: a table macro cannot take a row, so ov_to_pgr() reads every row of ov_segments_local,
-- and the loop over each segment's connectors becomes window functions in list order.
CREATE OR REPLACE MACRO ov_to_pgr() AS TABLE
WITH
segment AS (
SELECT
-- Carry over some attributes directly
id, geometry, class, subclass, names.primary AS primary_name,
-- Take the first surface we see rather than
-- chopping up the segment here
road_surface[1].value AS surface,
CAST(pgr_segment_kmph(speed_limits[1].max_speed.value, speed_limits[1].max_speed.unit, class) AS REAL) AS speed_kmph,
-- Overture uses "backward" access restrictions
-- for one-way segments, and the restriction can
-- show up anywhere in the list, so...
coalesce(list_bool_or([r.access_type = 'denied' AND r."when".heading = 'backward'
FOR r IN access_restrictions]), false) AS one_way,
connectors
FROM ov_segments_local
-- Chop segments into edges with vertexes at
-- the connectors. Each edge has two connectors
-- (one at each end) so a list of 3 connectors
-- implies outputting 2 edges.
listed AS (
SELECT s.* EXCLUDE (connectors), u.c.connector_id AS connector_id, u.c.at AS connector_to, u.i AS i
FROM segment AS s, unnest(s.connectors) WITH ORDINALITY AS u(c, i)
-- DuckDB: the loop starts from connector_to = 0.0 and then always holds the previous connector's
-- at, whether that connector was kept or skipped.
compared AS (
SELECT *,
CASE WHEN i = 2 THEN CAST(0.0 AS DOUBLE) ELSE lag(connector_to) OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY i) END AS connector_from
FROM listed
-- Avoid emitting zero-length segments
kept AS (
SELECT *, lag(connector_id) OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY i) AS connector_source
FROM compared
WHERE i = 1 OR connector_to <> connector_from
SELECT
id,
-- This is where we chop!
ST_LineSubstring(geometry, connector_from, connector_to) AS geometry,
connector_source, connector_id AS connector_target, class, subclass, surface, speed_kmph,
primary_name, one_way
FROM kept
WHERE i > 1;
-- Chop segments into edges, using the connectors list
-- and proportions. Extract other attributes like name
-- surface, speed and so on for easier access.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE pgr_segments AS
SELECT * FROM ov_to_pgr();
SELECT count(*) AS rows_created FROM pgr_segments;

presets.label: Vertices from connectors
sql: -- Next: “Routable edges”; the map draws the network once that has run too.
-- Extract the connector geometry from the connectors
-- list, materializing a new connector for each proportion.
-- Create an integer unique id for each connector while
-- where are at it.
-- DuckDB: there are no sequences. One row is kept per connector_id (its point taken from the
-- segment with the smallest id), then the ids are numbered by connector_id, so every run gives
-- the same ids.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE pgr_connectors AS
WITH connectors AS (
SELECT s.id, u.c.connector_id AS connector_id, ST_LineInterpolatePoint(s.geometry, u.c.at) AS geometry
FROM ov_segments_local AS s, unnest(s.connectors) AS u(c)
WHERE s.class IN ('motorway', 'primary', 'residential', 'secondary', 'tertiary', 'trunk', 'unclassified')
one_each AS (
SELECT connector_id, arg_min(geometry, id) AS geometry
FROM connectors
GROUP BY connector_id
SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY connector_id) AS vertex_id, connector_id, geometry
FROM one_each;
SELECT count(*) AS rows_created FROM pgr_connectors;

presets.label: Routable edges
sql: -- Next: “Connected components”, or straight to “Route between two points”.
-- Get the integer ids for the source/target connectors
-- for each edge, and add an integer edge id while we are
-- at it. Convert speed/length into cost, and ensure
-- one-way edges have negative cost.
-- DuckDB: the original's indexes are left out; DuckDB does not need them at this size.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE pgr_edges AS
SELECT
-- Assign a bigint unique id to the edge
-- DuckDB: row_number() over a stable order instead of a sequence, so every run gives the same ids.
row_number() OVER (ORDER BY seg.id, seg.connector_source, seg.connector_target) AS edge_id,
-- Lookup the bigint unique id for the source/target vertices
c1.vertex_id AS source_vertex_id,
c2.vertex_id AS target_vertex_id,
-- Calculate the cost
pgr_segment_cost(seg.geometry, seg.speed_kmph) AS cost,
-- Infinite cost when trying to travel a one-way street backwards
CASE WHEN one_way THEN -1 ELSE pgr_segment_cost(seg.geometry, seg.speed_kmph) END AS reverse_cost,
-- Will need the edge geometry to construct the spatial path
-- from the route edge sequence
seg.geometry,
ST_Length_Spheroid(ST_FlipCoordinates(seg.geometry)) AS length,
-- Carry over info from the overture tables
seg.id,
seg.connector_source,
seg.connector_target,
seg.class,
seg.subclass,
seg.surface,
seg.speed_kmph,
seg.primary_name,
seg.one_way
FROM pgr_segments seg
LEFT JOIN pgr_connectors c1 ON c1.connector_id = seg.connector_source
LEFT JOIN pgr_connectors c2 ON c2.connector_id = seg.connector_target
WHERE seg.class IN ('motorway', 'primary', 'residential', 'secondary', 'tertiary', 'trunk', 'unclassified')
AND c1.connector_id IS NOT NULL
AND c2.connector_id IS NOT NULL;
SELECT count(*) AS rows_created, count(*) FILTER (WHERE one_way) AS one_way FROM pgr_edges;

presets.label: Connected components
sql: -- Next: “Route between two points”.
-- Playground: pgRouting's connected components of the edges, largest first. A route exists only
-- between two vertices of one component, and one-way edges can still block it.
SELECT component, count(*) AS vertices
FROM pgr_connectedComponents(
'SELECT edge_id AS id, source_vertex_id AS source, target_vertex_id AS target, cost, reverse_cost FROM pgr_edges')
GROUP BY component
ORDER BY vertices DESC, component;

presets.label: Route between two points
sql: -- Next: “Route as GeoJSON”. “Pick start” and “Pick goal” on the map rewrite the two points below.
-- Ready to route!
-- Very simple implemenation of a routing function.
-- DuckDB: pgr_routeline() becomes statements. Table function arguments must be constants, so the
-- vertices pass through variables, and the route is kept as rows in the table route for the map
-- to draw; “Route as GeoJSON” returns the original's result.
-- Playground: the points are in Hiroshima (Hiroshima Station to Peace Memorial Park), not Victoria.
SET VARIABLE pt0 = ST_Point(132.4757, 34.3973);
SET VARIABLE pt1 = ST_Point(132.4528, 34.3925);
-- Lookup the nearest vertex to our start and end geometry
-- DuckDB: no <-> operator; ST_Distance is the same planar distance.
SET VARIABLE vertex0 = (SELECT vertex_id FROM pgr_connectors ORDER BY ST_Distance(geometry, getvariable('pt0')) LIMIT 1);
SET VARIABLE vertex1 = (SELECT vertex_id FROM pgr_connectors ORDER BY ST_Distance(geometry, getvariable('pt1')) LIMIT 1);
-- Playground: stop with a plain error rather than return an empty route. Each check sets a
-- variable rather than returning a row, because the Playground shows the first result of a script.
SET VARIABLE distinct_vertices = (SELECT CASE WHEN getvariable('vertex0') = getvariable('vertex1')
THEN error('Start and goal snap to the same vertex; pick points further apart.') END);
-- SQL to create a pgRouting graph
-- This is as simple as they come.
-- More complex approaches might
--  * scale cost based on class
--  * restrict edges based on box formed
--    by start/end points
--  * restrict edges based on class
-- Run the Dijkstra shortest path and join back to edges
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE route AS
SELECT d.seq, d.node, d.edge, d.cost, d.agg_cost, e.primary_name, e.class, e.speed_kmph
FROM pgr_dijkstra(
'SELECT
edge_id AS id,
source_vertex_id AS source,
target_vertex_id AS target,
cost, reverse_cost
FROM pgr_edges',
getvariable('vertex0'), getvariable('vertex1')) AS d
LEFT JOIN pgr_edges AS e ON e.edge_id = d.edge;
SET VARIABLE route_found = (SELECT CASE WHEN (SELECT count(*) FROM route) = 0
THEN error('No route: start and goal are in different components (see “Connected components”), or one-way edges block the way; pick other points.') END);
SELECT * FROM route ORDER BY seq;

presets.label: Route as GeoJSON
sql: -- Last step. For another route, pick new points and run “Route between two points” again; for
-- another area, press “Use this view” with “Choose the area” in the editor and start from there.
-- Run the Dijkstra shortest path and join back to edges
-- to create the path geometry
-- DuckDB: ST_Union_Agg is the aggregate that PostGIS spells ST_Union.
SELECT ST_AsGeoJSON(ST_Union_Agg(e.geometry)) AS geojson
FROM route
JOIN pgr_edges e
ON e.edge_id = route.edge;
